changes.title: Upcoming invoice endpoints replaced by Create Preview Invoice
changes.description: The Retrieve Upcoming Invoice (invoices.retrieveUpcoming) and List Upcoming Invoice Line Items (invoices.listUpcomingLines) endpoints were removed in API version 2025-03-31.basil. They are replaced by the Create Preview Invoice endpoint (invoices.createPreview), which returns the same preview invoice object; its line items are paginated via invoices.listLineItems on the returned preview, or read from preview.lines.

detect.notes: Parameters largely carry over: customer, subscription, subscription_items map to the same names on createPreview; subscription_* flat params moved under subscription_details in basil.

replace.guidance: Replace stripe.invoices.retrieveUpcoming(params) with stripe.invoices.createPreview(params). Move subscription_items/subscription_proration_date style params under subscription_details: { items, proration_date }. For listUpcomingLines, create the preview first and read its .lines, preserving any pagination the caller did.
replace.before: const upcoming = await stripe.invoices.retrieveUpcoming({ customer: customerId });
replace.after: const upcoming = await stripe.invoices.createPreview({ customer: customerId });

changes.title: Subscription current_period_start/end moved to subscription items
changes.description: In 2025-03-31.basil, the current_period_start and current_period_end fields were removed from the Subscription object. Billing periods are now tracked per subscription item: subscription.items.data[i].current_period_start / current_period_end. For single-item subscriptions, use the first item's period fields.

detect.notes: Only flag reads from a Subscription object; reads already on items.data[...] are the NEW pattern and must not be rewritten. If the variable is an invoice line or subscription item, it is not affected.

replace.guidance: Replace subscription.current_period_end with subscription.items.data[0].current_period_end (and same for _start) when the subscription has a single item, which is the common case; if the code manages multi-item subscriptions, compute the relevant item's period instead and note it in the manifest. Ensure the subscription fetch expands or includes items (stripe-node includes items.data by default up to 10 items).
